gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker SOLIX S5000's 120 V and 240 V outputs cannot be used at the same time (Anker's own product page), so a 240 V load on the L14-30R and 120 V plug-in loads cannot run together from its outlets, while EcoFlow's TITAN 5000 Classic has no 240 V output at all.
standout_why: Compared against four pages I opened: offgridcurrent.com whole-home guide (cited), thesolarlab.com big power stations, powerstations.reviews database (cited), and Jackery's product page as far as other pages quote it. OffGrid Current gives the S5000 as '4,500 W at 120/240 V' and says the TITAN 5000 Classic is '120 V only', but never mentions the either/or restriction, per-leg limits or split-phase for these units. The Solar Lab never covers the S5000 and gives only total inverter watts. powerstations.reviews has no voltage column and its visible text does not list the S5000. Held at 2 rather than 3 because the two other cited pages (Popular Mechanics S5000 review, Car and Driver roundup) could not be fetched, so I cannot rule out that Popular Mechanics states it.
decides: It splits the 5 kWh line by what the shopper plugs in. For 120 V essentials only (fridge, furnace blower, lights, internet) the restriction does not bite and the S5000 works. For a 240 V load running alongside 120 V loads from the unit's own outlets, the S5000 is either/or by Anker's statement, and the TITAN 5000 Classic is out by EcoFlow's statement (120 V only, 'not designed for 240V appliances like central AC, a well pump, or an electric dryer'). That confirms a 7,200 W 120/240 V unit (Jackery 5000 Plus, EcoFlow TITAN 5000 / 5000 Plus) as the pick for mixed loads. Separately, Anker's page today says S5000 orders ship within 15-16 weeks, which under the page's four-week rule keeps it from being the pick; it stays a listed row as the 240 V-capable unit at $2,499.99.

findings.label: 120 V and 240 V outputs at the same time
findings.value: Not supported: 'Please note: 120V and 240V outputs cannot be used simultaneously.'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 5kWh Solar Generator - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Maker's product-page FAQ, quoted as returned by the page fetch. The page describes no per-leg (L1/L2) limit, split-phase behaviour or neutral. It does not say what a transfer switch fed from the L14-30R gets on its 120 V circuits, so do not claim either way.

findings.label: Maximum output per outlet type
findings.value: 120 V NEMA 5-20R: 2,400 W; 120 V TT-30R: 3,600 W; 240 V L14-30R: 4,500 W; loads over 4,500 W trigger overload protection
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 5kWh Solar Generator - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Anker's FAQ says these apply 'regardless of input power' with bypass. The page gives no amp figures in text. My arithmetic: 4,500 W / 240 V = 18.75 A on the L14-30R, well under the receptacle's 30 A; 3,600 W / 120 V = 30 A on the TT-30R; 2,400 W / 120 V = 20 A on a 5-20R.

findings.label: Home connection, in Anker's words
findings.value: 'For essential circuit backup, connect it to your home electrical panel via a compatible transfer switch or power inlet box.'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 5kWh Solar Generator - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: The same page links the user guide at support.ankersolix.com/s/articlemanual?pn=AS510 (model number AS510).

findings.label: Price and dispatch notice
findings.value: $2,499.99 (list $3,599.99); 'Orders placed on or after November 25th will ship within 15 - 16 weeks.'; 97 lb
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 5kWh Solar Generator - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Standalone S5000 variant; Black Friday countdown on the page. 15-16 weeks is beyond the page's four-week rule for a pick.

findings.label: Third-party reading of the user guide (AS510)
findings.value: '120V or 240V, not both at once, per its user guide'; 'The outputs do not support simultaneous 120V and 240V output.'; all 120 V outlets together 4,500 W
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 vs EcoFlow TITAN 5000 Plus: Station on Wheels vs Home Battery (Backup Power Hub)
findings.note: Backup Power Hub attributes this to Anker's US product page and user guide. Use as corroboration only; the maker's own sentence is in the first finding.

findings.label: Voltage selection on the unit
findings.value: Separate '120V AC and 240V AC buttons above the outlets'; L14-30R described as 'A 120/240 V twist-lock, up to 4,500 W: the plug for a transfer switch or a generator inlet box'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 (2026): Specs, What It Runs, 51 Head-to-Heads (Station Arena)
findings.note: Station Arena's description, citing Anker's spec table and diagram. It also writes 'Four NEMA 5-20R outlets, up to 2,400 W in all', which reads differently from Anker's FAQ line (2,400 W for the 5-20R); it does not say whether the buttons are mutually exclusive.

findings.label: Output voltage
findings.value: 120 V only, 4 kW; 'is not designed for 240V appliances like central AC, a well pump, or an electric dryer'
findings.source_title: What Can EcoFlow TITAN Power? Output & Runtime Guide (EcoFlow US blog)
findings.note: Maker's blog, not the product page (us.ecoflow.com returned HTTP 429 three times today). The blog does not describe how the Classic connects to a home panel.

findings.label: Output
findings.value: '7.2kW of 120V/240V split-phase output for the home circuits you choose to back up'
findings.source_title: What Can EcoFlow TITAN Power? Output & Runtime Guide (EcoFlow US blog)
findings.note: EcoFlow says auto-switchover and circuit-level backup need Smart Home Panel 10, installed by a qualified electrician. No per-leg limit is given for this model.

findings.label: Per-leg 120 V output
findings.value: 'up to 5kW may be available on either 120V leg in a supported configuration'; 7.2 kW on battery alone, 'up to 10kW only when compatible solar panels are connected and producing'
findings.source_title: What Can EcoFlow TITAN Power? Output & Runtime Guide (EcoFlow US blog)
findings.note: EcoFlow adds that the per-leg figure does not mean every outlet can supply 5 kW. Backup Power Hub's comparison (read 2026-11-27) lists the same as 'X-Boost 2.0: up to 5kW on either 120V leg' with outlets '2 × NEMA 5-20R' and '1 × NEMA L14-50R'.

findings.label: 240 V port, as reported by a third party
findings.value: 'four standard 120V outlets plus one 120V/240V output (NEMA L14-30R/14-50, 30A)'; 7,200 W continuous
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus Review: The Ultimate Power Station (Backup Power Hub)
findings.note: Not read on Jackery's own page (HTTP 429 twice; Jackery FAQ HTTP 403). My arithmetic: 30 A × 240 V = 7,200 W, which implies 30 A × 120 V = 3,600 W per leg, but no source I opened states a per-leg limit for the Jackery, so do not print 3,600 W per leg as a maker figure.

findings.label: What the cited rival page says about these units' voltage
findings.value: OffGrid Current: S5000 '5,024 Wh and 4,500 W at 120/240 V in 97 lb'; TITAN 5000 Classic 'but 120 V only'; Jackery 'delivers 7,200 W at 120/240 V'. No mention of simultaneous 120/240 V use, per-leg limits or split-phase for these three.
findings.note: The rival baseline the standout score is judged against. The same page gives idle draw 8.8 W for the S5000 and 50 W standby for the Jackery.
